name: Víctor Gutiérrez García
role: PhD student in computer vision at GAPS-UPM

home.bio: I am a PhD student in the Signal Processing Applications Group (GAPS-UPM) at Universidad Politécnica de Madrid, advised by Dr. José Luis Blanco Murillo. My research focuses on efficient unsupervised image segmentation algorithms.
home.note: I received an MSc in Signal Processing and Machine Learning in 2025 and a BSc in Telecommunications Engineering in 2024 from UPM. Before starting my PhD, I worked on stockpile volume estimation for the DigiEcoQuarry project and developed radar tracking algorithms and simulations at Advanced Radar Technologies.

news.text: adapted for annotating long videos without running out of memory.

home.research: I am interested in computer vision, especially efficient networks for image and video segmentation, representation learning, and manifold learning.

publications.title: PANC: Prior-Aware Normalized Cut for Object Segmentation
publications.authors: Juan Gutiérrez, Víctor Gutiérrez, and José Luis Blanco
publications.description: A weakly supervised spectral segmentation method that injects a few annotated tokens into a token-affinity graph to guide normalized-cut clustering toward stable, controllable object masks.

publications.title: An Evaluation of Hybrid Annotation Workflows on High-Ambiguity Spatiotemporal Video Footage
publications.authors: Juan Gutiérrez, Víctor Gutiérrez, Ángel Mora-Sánchez, Silvia Rodríguez-Jiménez, and José Luis Blanco-Murillo
publications.description: An evaluation of assisted video annotation workflows using a fine-tuned vision-language model.

description: Worked on the European DigiEcoQuarry project, applying signal processing and computer vision to estimate stockpile volumes from video.

Developed radar simulation features, target classification, data visualization tools, and MATLAB tools for measurement post-processing.
Tutored high-school students in mathematics, physics, and chemistry.
